item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 13
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 13 twice.

This episode was all about what happened to the future Rudy who showed up in the previous episode. In the previous episode, there were no flashback scenes, just the two Rudies talking to each other, but in this episode, we were able to see what actually happened to the future Rudy. This was depressing and heartbreaking.

So, as expected, first Roxy got the petrification after a few cats or rats had been seen. And Cliff was the first to figure it out, and he also found out how and where to cure it. So Rudy, Cliff, and Zanoba went to the Millis church to get the sacred text. I thought they would get the god-class detoxification magic the official way, but they stole it! That was something unexpected. And of course they were chased, and on the way, Cliff got hurt and died. In the last episode, I wondered when he had died, but he died even before Roxy did. And he belonged to the Millis religion, but he even stole its bible to prioritize saving Roxy. I liked Cliff even more here, but I got sad when he died. Of course, Elinalise got mad at Rudy and hit him, but he was well aware that she had the right to do it. Anyway, Roxy was already dead when Rudy went back to his home.

Then Sylphie was trying to comfort him, but he couldn't recover from his depression. Without someone's help, he couldn't do it at all. And then, because he was depressed, he stopped by a brothel one night, but the next morning, Sylphie found him at the door. The future Rudy didn't mention this at all, probably because it was too pathetic for him to talk about. I guess she was worried about him and went looking for him, but it came back to haunt her. Anyhow, that was how she left him and joined the rebels in the Asura Kingdom. Rudy was still a complete mess, but when Rudy's mother slapped him, he decided to follow Sylphie and bring her back. But when he arrived at the Asura capital, all the rebels were dead, and Rudy saw all of them, including Sylphie, crucified. And I didn't notice at first, but she had lost her right arm too. And when he saw her, he flew into a rage and burned an entire kingdom completely. At this point, he was a real terrorist attacking Millis and Asura. The scene was cruel and depressing, but here, he crossed the line completely. He was emotional but I didn't expect he could do this.

After that, his life got even more messed up, and even Lilia gave up on fixing him and all of them left his mansion. He still went to the academy and built a robot that looked like Sylphie. He couldn't build Roxy? Probably he wanted to apologize and really wanted to make things right with Sylphie, so he tried to make her first, but it looked fragile. Anyhow, when I saw that, Zanoba and Julie built some really cool stuff, like an android. But it seemed he broke it by himself? Maybe he didn't want to see a fake her and insult her. He also helped Nanahoshi as he did before. However, Nanahoshi killed herself while he wasn't there. I was expecting him to be there for the last experiment, but he wasn't. It was such a regrettable thing.

But then, years later, Aisha came back to his mansion as an adult and helped him as a maid. She really loved her brother. So he wondered why he couldn't pull himself together after Roxy's death.

Then, he dreamed of Man God. And it told him that the displacement incident had changed the future. And Man God couldn't affect him, so it needed to gain his trust and eliminate Roxy. Once he heard that, he decided to find Man God and started searching the world. He met Eris and Ghislaine from time to time: when he was trying to save Roxy, when he went to Sylphie, and at other times. But she kept attacking him, and he was trying to get information about Man God even from her but of course he couldn't. He didn't really have any clue at that time. Then he didn't want to take the risk of talking to Perugius in case he was connected with Man God, so he decided to get information from Atofe. I don't understand why they started fighting. I guess he just turned down what Atofe said. Anyway, he couldn't defeat her. And then Eris saved him and was killed. At this point, at least 30 years had passed, and Eris and Ghislaine still followed him. She really couldn't find the right words to tell him, and kept loving him for more than three decades. During those years, Rudy couldn't think about much else because he was always occupied with the deaths of Roxy and Sylphie, and then with Man God. So there was no room in his mind for Eris.

Right before he fought against Atofe, his mansion was also attacked somehow, and Zanoba, Julie, and Aisha were killed too. It was still unclear why, but it seemed one of the kingdoms had attacked his mansion. Anyway, he apparently destroyed that kingdom for vengeance. So, at this point, he lost almost all of his family and friends. What it didn't show was what happened to Lilia, his mother, Norn, Elinalise, Sara, and demon's princesses. The rest of them died before they got old.

Then somehow, he found a place with a dragon mural, and he understood that the world had been made by combining six worlds. And Man God was in the center of those worlds, which basically had nothing. What were the six worlds? Demon world, human world, and what else? Or, maybe each God Style actually comes from a different world? Sword, North, Water, Dragon, and what else? Anyhow, he figured out 5 world items were required but needed a decade for each item, and he wouldn't live for that long. So, he got so strong and even cured his own arm with his magic, but he couldn't stop his aging with magic, unfortunately. And he decided to teleport himself into the past and he actually made it, as we saw in the last episode. In his last moment, he saw Sylphie and Roxy, and he saw them with his right eye, which can see the future. That didn't happen in the last episode, so he was able to see further into the future than current Rudy can, I guess.

Anyhow, since he came back to the past with teleportation magic, could that help Nanahoshi's experiment and make her magic successful? I wonder if Rudy will tell her about his future self. Also, Man God can influence many others, apparently, so that was the reason why the future Rudy told current Rudy that he shouldn't rely too much on others, because Man God can interfere. I guess Nanahoshi won't get affected, though. Demons like Roxy probably won't either. Then what will the world items be? I think collecting them and figuring out that dragon board (mural?) will be Rudy's goal. Also, what did Man God mean by "the future changed"? This guy obviously knows many scenarios of the future and also how to make them happen, so how could he not notice? Merging another world?

Music was good. At first, it was bright, but in a sad, depressing moment, the music stopped completely. Throughout this episode, the BGM was depressing or sad. Also, voice performance was pretty good in this episode. I liked Sylphie's voice performance in each scene, and also Man God when it laughed at Rudy and enjoyed it viciously.

Anyhow, will Rudy contact Eris, ask Nanahoshi for help, or maybe try to stop the civil war in the Asura Kingdom? I don't know what will come.

Scores

  • Episode: 10/10
  • Rudeus: 3/10
    • Well, I know he was depressed, but I kinda rated him lower in this episode. But I guess he is a normal person who can get devastated and can be even evil if the worst thing happens
  • Eris: 9/10
    • She had faith in him for decades. Okay, I really liked these kinds of characters.
  • Ghislaine: 10/10
    • This woman protected and served Eris for all those years and even saved Rudy. Cool.
  • Cliff: 9/10
    • I like a person who puts his friends before his own beliefs
  • Aisha: 8/10
    • Even Lilia, who had been grateful to him since she gave birth to Aisha, gave up on Rudy, but Aisha believed he would get back on his feet, and she came back.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 12
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 12 twice.

So, this episode was almost entirely about the talk between the current and future Rudy. What happened to the future Rudy was pretty horrible. First, Roxy died. I had wondered what would have happened if Rudy had gone to the basement. There was a rat in the basement, and the rat gave her the illness that killed her. I didn't expect that a little thing would kill somebody, but it was actually similar to Nanahoshi's mana illness. Also, Roxy had a baby in her belly and that caused it. So, it sounded like Man God wanted to kill Roxy or her baby, though old Rudy couldn't figure out its intent.

Next, Sylphie died. Because she couldn't get Rudy back on his feet after Roxy's death, she left to join the civil war in the Asura Kingdom and died. Luke was also tricked by Man God. So, not only Rudy but also other people were manipulated by it.

Then he fought against Eris again and again, and she died too. Nanahoshi's experiment also failed, and she died. It sounded like Cliff wasn't alive, but I don't know when he died. So overall, his life at the end was full of regret, after a few weeks of the same time in this episode. And that might've been the reason why he said he wasn't Rudy.

I also thought old Rudy knew who Man God was, but even he didn't know. At least he was named as Human God and now Man God, and also he said Man God couldn't be defeated. It was so convincing because he could even use a lot of strong magic like time travel, flying, or telepathy and still couldn't find it. Will the Rudy in this world win against it? I don't know. But as old Rudy said, Man God is the last boss, so he might be able to. But because of the time travel, old Rudy lost part of his body, and he was also near his end. But right before he died, he sensed Roxy and Sylphie over the wall, meaning he was also able to see things through obstacles like walls.

Rudy went out of the room and talked to them, but of course, he couldn't tell them what had really happened. He actually also followed what old Rudy said, because he said he shouldn't rely too much on others. I felt it was weird, but he lived by himself for a long time, so that might be the reason he said so. Anyhow, Roxy accepted that there was something he couldn't tell her, and they just went back to their rooms and decided not to leave their rooms that night. And Rudy just burned old Rudy's body and buried his bones in the ground. Then he decided to go to the basement and used ice magic before going in. And he found a frozen mouse with teeth made of petrified mana in the basement, as old Rudy guessed. Old Rudy also gave the diary to Rudy, and that's for the next episode.

So the next episode is probably what happened to the old Rudy, and it's going to be a horrible thing, I believe.

Scores

  • Episode: 8/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • It was great to see both old Rudy, who was full of regret, and Rudy, who saw that man and made up his mind that he didn't want to be like him.
  • Roxy: 8/10
    • She is an understanding girl. When Rudy can't tell her something, she accepts it without complaining.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 11
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 11 twice.

Because Rudy had a nightmare about Atofe, I thought Atofe would become another trauma for Rudy, but it seems not.

Nanahoshi got completely better. She needs to drink tea made from sokas grass every day to keep her illness away, but anyway, she got better and she was really grateful to Rudy. She had slapped him last time, but he forgave her anyway, and she even started showing him respect for the first time. They got along even better, and she wondered what his previous life was like, but he didn't want to talk about it. Well, he was nothing like the current Rudy back then, so it totally makes sense.

Then Cliff got a reward from Kishirika: a right eye like Rudy's, but its ability is to see all kinds of information about each person. He didn't say what kinds of information, but can he see whether Rudy was reincarnated from another world? I don't know. Maybe that wasn't a big issue either way.

Then Perugius started to like Rudy. He really hated demons, and the blow he dealt Atofe in the last episode was so good for him without him risking anything. Because he was able to get a chance to do so thanks to Rudy and Zanoba, he came to like them. I hadn't noticed that he didn't rely on or trust Rudy that much before, though. Maybe because his magic seemed like Laplace's? Zanoba also talked with Perugius a lot, and he also knew Ruijerd had saved Perugius before. Rudy was impressed when Zanoba talked about it, and it seemed he had forgotten it, so he tried to bring Ruijerd up with Perugius. Anyway, as a reward for dealing with Atofe, he got something from Perugius that he can use to call him. And I thought Princess Ariel was just sitting there, but when she brought up that she could bring statues, Perugius wasn't really interested in it. And instead, he asked her a question and she couldn't answer. The question was "What is the quality of a king?" What was that answer? I recalled something from Ling Yao from Fullmetal Alchemist, and it sounded similar to what Rudy said.

Anyhow, Rudy went back to his home, and hugged Roxy as he promised. Husband and wife moment. Then he talked about what happened and then he wrote a diary, and then Man God came to his dream. I knew because the title of this episode was "Turning Point 4." Then he talked about what would've happened if he had followed what Man God said. And everyone, including Roxy and his father, would've been saved. This sounded terribly wrong. Without him, Roxy would've been dead for sure in the dungeon. There was no way Paul and the others could've defeated the hydra without her and Rudy. So, they would probably all have died, or at least some of them would have. Anyway, Man God asked Rudy for a favor this time, which sounded pretty small. Because Rudy has a high EQ and felt sorry for Man God, he wanted to do what Man God said. At the end, Man God showed a creepy, vile smile in the animation, but it could still be just a misleading scene. Anyhow, Rudy was trying to go to his sanctuary in order to find something unusual, as Man God had told him. But then, an old guy came into the room out of the blue and told Rudy that he was from the future, proving it by saying Rudy's name from his previous life. I hadn't realized Rudy had never told anyone his name from his previous life, but now thinking about it, he only talked about the past life to Nanahoshi, and he didn't really want to talk about it, so there was no way anybody could know. And old Rudy said he had been deceived by Man God, but that was where the episode ended.

I don't know what will happen if he enters the basement. In the first place, what was the "something unusual"? And also, who is Man God? My guess is that Man God is actually Laplace, because that name has come up so many times so far. And Man God was actually sealed like Perugius said, so he was trying to come back to life. Also, that means just like he tricked Ruijerd's people, he was trying to trick Rudy. I don't know what the "something unusual" was. But maybe it could take over Rudy's body so that Man God could come back into the world. Then probably starting a war or something? Even if he wasn't Laplace, he sure was a legendary person like Orsted or Perugius and could cause a devastating result.

Anyway, what will the next episode be about? Old Rudy will talk about what will happen in the future, and Rudy will choose not to do that. But the title is "An End and a Beginning," so something big will start for sure.

Scores

  • Episode: 9/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • He kept his promise to Roxy.
    • He was also trying to do his best in this life
  • Zanoba: 8/10
    • Okay, I started liking him more and more. This guy is great
  • Perugius: 8/10
    • This guy might be legendary but this guy is definitely a person.
  • Man God: 4/10
    • He has been so suspicious, but in this episode, he kinda showed his true self for a moment.
    • At least he was a natural-born liar
    • Let's see how much of a scumbag this guy is.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 10
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 10 twice.

When Kishirika tried to surprise everybody by saying there was no sokas grass, they were about to get mad but tried not to show it. Their faces were so twisted, and it was funny. And of course, Cliff was the first to say it while Rudy was trying to hold it back. Then soldiers came and Moore spoke the human language instead of the demon tongue. I thought he was a human, but it seems I was wrong.

They went to the Demon King's tower, which was a good one, a tower with a spiral staircase. Rudy and Zanoba went to the throne to hand over Kishirika, while Cliff and Elinalise went to find the sokas grass. When Rudy met the Immortal Demon King, Atofe, she turned out to be a selfish and arrogant king who never listened to anyone. Kishirika actually warned them earlier so she was right. All the soldiers, Rudy, and Zanoba tried to stop her and were blown away. It looks like she was so strong, and she had lost only twice, to her husband Kalman, who was the North God, and to Laplace, so most of her soldiers were those people who couldn't flee from her. How sad they were. Anyhow, Moore allowed Rudy to leave with Kishirika.

But then Atofe was waiting for them in front of the warp gate. So, Rudy and Elinalise planned how to fight her, and decided to let Cliff leave the place and ask Perugius to help them. In the fight scene, and in this episode, Zanoba was so strong. Was he this strong all along? I didn't remember but he was so tough that even Atofe couldn't move. And it was interesting that the one Rudy couldn't stop wasn't Atofe, but Moore. He said he was a master of magic so he recognized how skillful he was. He used ice magic, quagmire, Disturb Magic, and even lightning, which even hurt his own side. But it couldn't completely stop them, but he was enough to stop.

Then, Perugius came to the place and used his magic on Atofe because it was a good chance for him. What happened to them? Was he angry with her or something? He knew it wouldn't kill her completely and he didn't intend to break the pact, so he wasn't serious. So, I didn't get what he was trying to do here.

Anyway, I feel like this fight can cause something bigger later. The next episode will be "Turning Point 4", so something big will happen in the next episode, or at least the next few episodes.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • In this episode, he showed a full range of expressions. He was frustrated, got scary, and was relieved.
  • Zanoba: 7/10
    • He is mature, mentally strong, and calm. How reliable he is.
    • And he is so tough and strong.
  • Kishirika: 5/10
    • Well, this is a kid.
    • It was interesting to see an animation of her right eye and it rotated to figure out who Rudeus was.
  • Perugius: 7/10
    • Did he hate the demon a lot?
  • Atofe: 5/10
    • She doesn't listen to whatever anyone else says. Stubborn woman. Also, she made others wait for 2 hours.
    • This king might be crazily strong in a fight scene, though
  • Moore: 4/10
    • What did he think? He gave Rudy some advice, but then he knew how it would turn out. I don't know what his aim was

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 18
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 18 twice.

The Volcanica Emilia faced was like an NPC in a game. It just kept repeating the same lines and tried to protect the pillar behind it. When Emilia got close to the pillar, she had to fight it. She used ice magic to create and summon her knights, and all of them are Subaru. She's a girl in love.

Subaru and Meili were fighting against Shaula's scorpion. And I wondered how he would fight it, but he was just trying to stop the scorpion, maybe unless it doesn't resist them? But the scorpion's attack shot Meili in the stomach. It seemed that Subaru would take on her damage with his new authority, Cor Leonis, but no such scene was animated.

The entire rest of this episode was about the fight between Ram and Gluttony. Subaru got his new authority, Cor Leonis, so he was able to take Ram's burden instead, and Ram was able to keep fighting against Gluttony. When did he remember this authority and how? There was no such scene. Maybe he learned it when the two of them merged, or while he was in the Corridor of Memories?

Anyhow, Ram was able to fight a lot longer than she used to. In the past, she lost her mana and stamina very quickly and couldn't fight for a long time at all. And knowing this, after fighting for a short period, Gluttony went to where Rem was, because he thought she couldn't catch up with him. But she was able to catch up with him and hit him. However, he was able to transform into Rem and she was blown away and then her rod was broken. But then, she realized that she and Rem shared everything, too. And it looks like the rod itself was actually made from her original horn? So, after that, she used Rem's power to fight him. She was originally a genius among the demons, so she overwhelmed him completely.

The fight scene between them was great. I wondered why they could fly so easily, but Ram can use her wind magic so she can fly and it made the fight interesting, especially on the huge spiral staircase in the tower. I didn't get what he drew on the wall at the end, but maybe it was love or something? Anyway, he got what he deserved. Because he pulled some memories from his body, does that mean many people's memories were back? Also, Ram's memories of Rem were coming back and her feelings toward Rem were coming back, too, even though it was not complete in this episode.

Also, I'd always wondered what Ram was thinking back when her horn was broken. Rem thought it was finally broken and was kinda relieved, and Rem blamed herself all along in her life for that relief. But Ram thought the same thing. Because Ram and Rem shared emotions and so on, as Ram explained in this episode, Ram might've also felt what Rem thought. Rem always thought and said Ram was the best, and Ram was proud of herself too, for example.

So, there are still 2 things remaining: Emilia's exam in the tower and Subaru fighting against the scorpion to break Shaula's curse. Will these be resolved? Also, will the memories of Julius and Emilia come back, and will Rem wake up? Those things should happen in the next episode.

Scores

  • Episode: 9/10
    • This episode is one of the best episodes for Ram. And also the episode for Ram and Rem. There was another best episode for her in season 2, but this episode also included her past.
  • Emilia: 8/10
    • She is a girl who loves Subaru. Her magic gets creative too.
  • Ram: 9/10
    • She was no longer the girl who gets wiped out after using magic, thanks to Subaru and Rem.
    • She defeated one of the Sin Archbishops by herself. Wasn't that a little too strong?
  • Gluttony: 6/10
    • What is this guy? But doing something others hate the most was the most classic villain thing he did.
    • This guy made Re:Zero interesting and entertaining til season 4 so he should be rewarded based on that.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 17
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 17 twice.

The episode finally started the loop where Subaru would overcome the obstacles. The first thing Subaru did was go meet Emilia. She was so happy, and she kicked what's-his-name, who quickly fled from her. Wait, why did he escape that fast while in the other loops Subaru couldn't make him leave and had to fight him for a long time? Then Subaru met Beatrice and Ram and they talked about the tactics there. Emilia's actions were also so cute, especially when she pressed her cheek against Beatrice's.

Next, Subaru went to a place with Shaula, Meili, and Foxidna. I thought he would prevent Shaula from becoming the scorpion, but he couldn't prevent it. But instead, Emilia kicked the scorpion and made it fall to the ground from the tower, but that scorpion climbed up quickly to the balcony again. I wondered what the strategy was, but somehow, Subaru, Meili, and Beatrice would deal with the scorpion by riding the mabeast like a centaur while Meili was controlling it. And they climbed down from the tower and of course the scorpion followed Subaru. I was like, wait, was it okay to leave the tower, but Shaula had already become the scorpion so it didn't matter. But I still didn't know his strategy.

On the other side, Roy climbed upstairs while he couldn't reach out to Rui and Ley, but he didn't care about it. He was totally okay with being alone and fighting against Subaru and others, well, maybe because he thought he was strong enough? Then Ram was waiting for him. Of course, Subaru or Ram was the one who would fight and defeat Gluttony, thinking about Rem and the entire story in Re:Zero so far.

Then, Julius fought against Reid. I wondered how Julius got to where Reid was. In this loop, Subaru didn't tell him to go battle against Reid, if I remember correctly. Maybe he found Roy while moving around? Emilia also went there, but Reid didn't remember her, so Roy's authority affected Reid too. I thought in the first loop where she was forgotten, Reid might've remembered her, but I was wrong. Anyway, then because she passed the exam, she kept climbing up the tower, and that was Subaru's biggest bet in this loop, I think. Julius was fighting against Reid alone while Foxidna was just watching him. I guessed he was going to get his spirits' power back, but I expected he would do so after they defeated Gluttony. So, he just re-contracted with them right then and got his power back. The reason he could do it now, when he couldn't in the previous loops, was probably that Foxidna was there — she passed on what Subaru wanted her to tell him — and also his conversation with Reid. The fight animation between them started with free-moving camera angles, and it sometimes felt slow or even stopped, but it still showed how fast and intense the battle was. But I still imagined he couldn't defeat the Sword Saint, but the ending was kinda good and logical. The last blow seemed to kill Julius but it didn't, fortunately. That's why Julius admitted, at that moment, that Reid had won the battle. Also, Anastasia was back in that scene. Foxidna had known all along why she was hiding, but she reached out to Anastasia so she could watch Julius at the top of his game. The reason why she hid was she couldn't bear losing her memories of Julius. Well, had she really never lost anything important in her life before? Anyway, right before she forgot him, she shouted his name while he was fighting against Reid at the last blow. Then they introduced themselves to each other because he knew she had forgotten him.

I think what Subaru bet was if Emilia could pass all the tower's exams, Shaula would get back from the scorpion. That's the one thing he needed to clear, and there may not have been any other solution. That was why Emilia was the key. In the next episode, because the title is "Ram", the story will mainly be about Ram vs. Gluttony, I guess. But I don't think it will end there, because defeating this Sin Archbishop would probably be the last of this arc so before that, Emilia would solve Shaula's curse, and Shaula's problem would end?

Scores

  • Episode: 9/10
  • Emilia: 9/10
    • In this episode, she was so happy and pressing her cheek against Beatrice's was also cute
  • Julius: 8/10
    • He was a commoner but tried to behave the way he wanted to be. The more episodes go by, the more I like him
  • Anastasia: 6/10
    • Hmm...? Did you really stop coming out over just one terrible thing?
  • Reid: 7/10
    • This guy was a great villain because he was one of the strongest characters.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 9
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 9 twice.

So, this episode reminded me of the episode when Nanahoshi became hysterical when her summoning magic failed at once. In this episode, because she thought she was going to die, she got hysterical again. It was because she really missed her original world and wanted to do what she wanted to do. She also didn't like that world because she hadn't aged at all. This was something other series don't care about, but in reality, this should be a problem. A person can easily die in an unfamiliar place from an unfamiliar virus or whatever, and that cannot be healed by magic. That's actually a pretty good detail in the story. It also rings true that empty words mean nothing to a person who is desperate. By the way, Nanahoshi's drawings are more realistic, like her mouth or fingers, maybe to show she has a medical issue?

Why didn't Perugius allow Rudy to check the archive? He said he didn't allow outsiders to go there, but is there any important book or something there?

The reason Perugius couldn't leave the fortress was that Laplace would come back. When that happened and Laplace attacked humans with his demons, then he would need to stop him. Because of that, he couldn't move and couldn't save Nanahoshi. So, Rudy travelled to the Demon Continent to meet Kishirika, because she was alive 7,000 years ago and she might know about the illness of the first person who didn't have mana and be dead. I wonder why humans got more mana 7,000 years ago and overcame the illness?

Anyhow, Rudy went to Rikarisu, which is a demon city. I didn't expect that Nokopara, the horse man, had been a friend of Roxy's before and Elinalise met with him. He somehow liked and trusted Roxy, so he wasn't going to trick any friend of hers. Coming back to the Demon Continent and seeing these characters made me feel nostalgic. And also, Kishirika hasn't changed a bit, but the animation was upgraded, so it was kinda... fun? I don't know.

Laplace is gathering demons and will start a war against humans, and Rudy is going to the Demon Continent. Is that some kind of sign that the war between demons and humans will start shortly? I don't know. In the next episode, I guess Rudy will meet the Demon King Artole and Kishirika, and maybe solve Nanahoshi's problem? Let's see.

Scores

  • Episode: 8/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • One great thing for Rudy is he isn't only positive, he empathizes with someone who is disappear and the reason behind it.
  • Nanahoshi: 8/10
    • It was a great, and sad scene when she cried out. I wonder whether she was going to be out or not
    • Her voice actress nailed the scene. That was amazing.
  • Cliff: 6/10
    • He has believed in Millis all along, and tried to take action, and got mad when someone didn't
  • Perugius: 7/10
    • It seems he is reliable
  • Nokopara: 5/10
    • No feeling, but a little bit plus as he does like Roxy

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 8
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 8 twice.

Alright. Finally the story started changing a little. It's a little interesting that demons aren't allowed in the flying fortress because Perugius doesn't like them. Because of that, Roxy wasn't allowed in. I guess she headed back by road on her own afterward because nobody was with her, and she knew it could take days. The reason why Rudy took time to be teleported was... Man God? Or the capacity of the magic? The teleport magic's animation reminded me of the background when Rudy met Man God.

Rudy also avoided answering, when he and Sylphie were asked, whether he knew Man God or not. She answered she didn't know, and I wondered whether she had just lied. Obviously, he lied because he had been attacked by Orsted the last time he answered that he knew. And they didn't have a way to recognize it. But I guess she didn't have such an experience, so she answered honestly. And in that case, why were they detected? Because of their magic capacity? Or magic without an incantation was detected, and they thought that was the handiwork of Man God, though Rudy figured it out by himself and taught her? Or, Rudy was actually created by Man God?

Anyhow, the flying fortress was a huge castle with nature inside it, and then they entered the throne room and met Perugius. He was intimidating, and many people were nervous, but Nanahoshi was calm and didn't hesitate to push back at him. Perugius was definitely a good guy. He also reacted to a couple of things: one was the fully autonomous doll, and the other was Rudy and Sylphie. I didn't know the intent behind naming their son if they had one, but did he have some intentions to bring Rudy and Sylphie onto his side? But why only a son? Zanoba's fully autonomous doll was rare even for him, so probably that fortress wasn't really industrialized. He also didn't know about the displacement incident. He thought it wasn't by humans, but was it really? I thought someone like Man God did it.

Also, we finally got to know why Elinalise got her curse. She was found in a labyrinth without her memory and emotions, and got emotions afterward, but never got her memories back. Even though she was married, her husband was killed and she needed to deal with her curse. And she needed to leave the elf village that had taken her in, because of her curse. Rudy empathized with her even though she hid her past, and this reminded me what a good character Rudy was. Rudy's past life was not going well.

Anyhow, then they talked about taking a lecture on teleport magic from Nanahoshi's master. And at lunch, they ate food similar to Japanese food. Because Nanahoshi really wanted to go back to her world, she shed tears while eating it, and I empathized with her. Then Cliff and Zanoba found a path to the underground, and some murals. But what were they? The Armored Dragon King immediately came and kicked them out. Did they mean something? He didn't say so, but were they murals from Laplace's time or something?

Also, Rudy was advised not to use his magic in the fortress. But Sylphie, who uses the same kind of magic as him, used hers when Nanahoshi came to their room because she was coughing a lot. Sylphie felt a little weird when she used her magic and tried to use more. But then Nanahoshi threw up blood. I didn't know it was because of her magic, or it was because of Nanahoshi's health, but probably the former. That place wasn't a good place to use magic for Sylphie or Rudy.

So, in the next episode, something will start happening. I want to see what's going to happen. They'll probably save Nanahoshi and come down from the flying fortress.

Scores

  • Episode: 8/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • He was calm down from a few facts, he looked worried when he met Perugius, so I felt his sense of anxiety which is usual for normal people.
  • Sylphie: 8/10
    • She didn't want Rudy to be too close to Nanahoshi and she was jealous. It was cute.
  • Nanahoshi: 8/10
    • She might be the anime character who most wants to go back to her own world. I liked this.
    • She also pushed back at Perugius, so that was good.
  • Perugius: 5/10
    • He seems like a nice person, but he's still a king, or a god.
  • Elinalise: 7/10
    • Finally, we've seen why she got a curse
  • Zanoba: 6/10
    • I liked his attitude and how frankly he talked with Perugius.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 7
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 7 twice.

This episode was the one about the natural progression of academy life, which was graduation. The main focus of the graduation was Linia and Pursena. In order to decide who would lead their tribes, they fought. Rudy was just excited and enjoyed watching the fight, though he didn't expect them to go their separate ways afterward. The fight took a long time, but the animation wasn't good. They mostly animated only a few specific characters, or shot the fight from a long distance. Maybe the production saved effort in this episode because it wasn't an important fight. Anyhow, they were worried about going their separate ways, but it seemed like they met immediately after they departed the city, so they were still really like glue.

Another important part was Nanahoshi's experiment. Rudy kept helping her and this time, he felt the summoning magic was similar to the mass teleportation in the past. The animation effects were at first really similar to that, but then they changed, and what it summoned turned out to be a big watermelon. Nanahoshi also got sick often. Does this indicate something about the future, like she was going to disappear because she was summoned from another world and didn't fit into that world? Or was this just showing the details of this world?

For some reason they celebrated shortly after, and at the celebration, Roxy got drunk and sat on Rudy's lap. She was so cute. Norn also wanted to join the student council and she asked Rudy if it was okay for her to join. At first, I wondered why she asked, but then I realized she thought he would worry about her not doing well in her writing and sword training. Anyhow, Sylphie helped her and told him that Norn had already been helping the student council. So he made a sensible decision and allowed her to do it.

Then, right at the end, Nanahoshi told Rudy that her master might know how to cure his mother. I didn't see this coming, so that was Rudy's next move, but it was actually a pretty natural thing for him to do. Then she told him who her master was: one of the three heroes who defeated Laplace. How could she know that kind of person? Well, we'll probably find that out shortly. So, on to the next episode, which will probably start a new arc.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
    • This was all preparation for the upcoming arc.
  • Rudeus: 7/10
  • Roxy: 9/10
    • So adorable to sit on Rudy's lap while she was plastered
  • Sylphie: 8/10
  • Nanahoshi: 8/10
    • She got sick and showed her fragility.
  • Linia: 5/10
  • Pursena: 5/10
  • Norn: 7/10
    • She started doing a few things well, so we knew she was putting in the effort. We're like her parents, watching her grow.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 6
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 6 twice.

This episode was mostly between Rudy and Sara. Sara, and how he parted ways with her, was one issue Rudy hadn't solved until this episode. So the main focus in this episode was to solve it, and it started with Sylphie's kid and Rudy. Honestly, I didn't recognize Suzanne at first, but once I did, it made sense that she had quit being an adventurer and gotten married. And she even got a job as a nanny at Rudy's house. Then, obviously, Rudy met Sara on the next job, but he avoided her, or ran away from her. I was a little pissed off. Why would he do that? But then he talked with her about the past and what happened, and showed how mature he had become. In terms of Sara, she felt a little sad after talking to Rudy, and I thought she had regrets. She might have, but after talking to Rudy she understood why it couldn't have worked, and she moved on. And then she and Rudy really became good friends. I liked her.

Other than that, Roxy was so welcomed by the party and so respected. I felt it was off that Rudy didn't do much during the fight and just stayed still, but I guess he let his guard down because Roxy was there.

Princess Ariel was a little involved and did one thing for Rudy, and more for Sylphie. That one thing was how considerate she was. Sylphie was like a worrier, and she accepted too much. Or at least when I heard what she said, she sounded more like Rudy's mom than his wife.

From Eris's point of view, I didn't expect Nina to be able to use the Blade of Light. But somehow, because of desire or resolve, Eris's Blade of Light was superior to Nina's. Eris took a hit, but she was able to strike Nina's opening and blew her all the way into a wall. Eris showed that she was putting her energy into her wooden sword, but at the same time, she was smiling softly by thinking about Rudy, and that was quite a good attitude. It obviously showed how she had leeway while Nina rushed a little and lost.

Because Princess Ariel was a little involved, I felt like a new story would start. But I don't know. Maybe... a war will come?

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • I already forgot why he still had the hots for Eris
  • Roxy: 8/10
    • She was our goddess.
  • Sylphie: 6/10
    • Her dedication to Rudy was... too convenient for the story.
  • Eris: 7/10
    • As always, she is stubborn. But she only cared about a few things.
  • Nina: 6/10
    • Sounded like she had high hopes of reaching a higher position like the Sword King.
  • Sara: 8/10

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 5 twice. 8/10. It seemed like this episode was meant to wrap up what happened after Rudeus came back to his mansion from the labyrinth.

Elinalise settled down with Cliff, instead of staying an adventurer. Cliff is a member of the Milis Church, but I don't think she is. I forgot about it, but she has a curse. How can she deal with it?

Also, the episode explained that there was no wedding of Rudeus and Roxy because the Migurd don't have that custom. So, this was the first episode that Roxy dressed up in something special at the wedding of Cliff and Elinalise, and it was so cute. She looked like a very cute kid.

Then what Rudy didn't do was throw Norn and Aisha their birthday celebrations. And he had a good memory and remembered the promise he had made with Paul about throwing a big party. And now he was responsible as the head of the Greyrats, so he planned and prepared it. When he was fishing with Norn, Aisha, and Roxy, he couldn't catch any fish, just a boot, so he cast a spell to catch fish. Even Roxy was a little disgusted with him. So, he had grown up a lot as the head of the Greyrats, but he still showed his childish side.

Roxy, on the other hand, still had a couple of challenges. Well, she was more like an introvert. Norn had a problem with her being Rudy's second wife, so Roxy wanted to get along with her, and fishing was her chance. I think she liked helping others, so it worked well and she taught Norn a few techniques. Also, she couldn't buy a hat when she found a good one. It was because the hat was too expensive. And Rudy and Sylphie bought and gave it to her as a wedding gift. That conversation between Sylphie and Roxy was, well, the polygamy point of view, so it was still kinda off to a monogamous person. But Sylphie really loved Rudy, and she was thankful to Roxy too. Roxy may still have felt awkward around her as the second wife, so I guess that was another thing she solved in the scene. Roxy's animation when she got the new hat from Sylphie was very detailed and well framed, so some of the animators must have liked this scene.

Zenith's behavior also improved a little, and she patted Norn's head and held Lilia's hand. Though, I don't know whether she'll ever fully recover, or when. Was her condition caused by magic, or by some other power? No idea how she'll turn out later.

I don't know what'll happen in the next episode. Apparently, Sara will show up again, so Rudy will probably get a job, maybe taking one from a guild. More than that, no idea. And I also have no idea when Rudy'll meet Eris next.
